sth_jonathan.text: Jonathan raises his head, weighs you up with great seriousness, and goes back to the grass. He is about 190. He has seen everything and has chosen not to comment.

then.text: You have said hello to Jonathan. He has not said hello back, which is how he says it.

sth_gardener.text: Jonathan eats the lawn, and a fair number of cabbages, and the occasional hat. He's a hundred and ninety, near enough. He's lost his sense of smell and some of his sight, but he knows when it's lunch.

We feed him a mix of lettuce, cucumber and bananas. He gets a sunny spot, and in the evenings he is brought in. The vet visits and says he is in great health for his age, which is not a lot of use as a figure.

then.text: Our wirebird is yours to remember. Keep to the paths.
A Wirefoot! One of ours, and you've got it in your Fieldbook. The curator will be pleased. You're on the list of friends.

else.text: Not yet. Look in the long grass on Deadwood Plain. Quiet feet, quiet voice.
The wirebird runs, rather than flies, and the island has fewer than a thousand. Keep your dog on a lead and your steps on the path, and we've a chance.

sth_consul.text: Longwood House has the rooms as Napoleon left them, as near as we can. The billiard room, the study, the bedroom where he died. The damp was terrible. The place was thought a miserable spot even in his day.
People ask if he was a prisoner. The island's records say so. The wallpaper says he was bored. Both are probably right.

sth_walker.text: The Diana's Peak walk is the one. Up through the tree-fern forest, cool and green, past the endemic whitewood and the dogwood. Wear a coat. The cloud comes down suddenly.
The tree ferns look like they walked out of a Jurassic picture book, and they've been here a lot longer than the Saints.

sth_mourner.text: The grave is empty and the willows are not. A great many people come to stand here, and say nothing. It is the most peaceful place on the island, which is quite an achievement for a ruined Emperor.

then.text: You came back for more! Monsieur or Madame is welcome at Longwood any time.

Bonjour. I am the French Honorary Consul, and I keep the keys. Our flag is the only one on the island that is not British, and I defend it. You have done the tour: a fight, then, in the French manner, with elegance and a little arrogance.
Bravo. You have the spirit of a marshal. Tell the curator the Consul says you may call yourself a Saint.

else.text: Bonjour. I keep the keys to Longwood, and I only fight those who have done the whole tour. Greet the tortoise, meet the wirebird, and bow at the empty tomb in Sane Valley. Then come back to me.

Bonjour. This is Longwood, a little piece of France on a British island. If you wish to be shown the island, the curator at the museum in Jamestown will begin the tour.
